title: Larkfield Party Co. event promo catalog + shelf-tag merge: neutralize eight mixed-light product shots to an in-frame grey card, author-a-colorway variant of the hero, prep and vectorize the wordmark, then data-merge the client's overset-safe auto-fit templates into press-ready catalog and price-tag PDFs
grounding_note: Adapted from a real freelance-marketplace brief and laundered to a fictional client, 'Larkfield Party Co.' (an event / party-supply promotion brand) — no real company, product, marketplace, software, or trademark is named in any task-facing field. The original brief's literal ask was to BUILD a page-layout plugin that 'automatically reduces font sizes if a record is too long for the frame', because merged text runs overset / gets clipped on export — that is a from-scratch software-development job, out of scope for any design connector. REPOSITIONED for connector reality and REPAIRED against the audit: (audit G1 — broken merge path) the prior version ran a pdf-to-layout conversion and then merged into the converted file (fields will not bind) and tried to bind the vector logo through a TEXT-ONLY vector-merge column (it cannot carry an image); both are removed. (audit G2 — batch amputated to one hero) the prior version prepped a single hero photo and called it 'a repeatable recipe', which deletes the one hardest, most gradeable thing — cross-asset color consistency; the batch is restored to eight differently-lit product shots, each with an in-frame 18% grey card. The overset problem is handled the honest way the connector can: the client authors BOTH print templates in a professional page-layout program with the program's native auto-size / shrink-to-fit text frames already enabled on the variable-data frames and live merge fields wired up, so the layout itself is overset-safe; the agent cannot 'fix overset' itself and must instead route field-matched data and prepped art into those authored templates. Invented concrete products (an eight-SKU party/event promo line, one card per SKU plus a matching shelf price tag) because the vertical is 'Party, Events & Promotion' and the source gives no specific product; field names, CSV columns, and bleed/size numbers are reasonable trade-print conventions, not taken from the brief. No plugin is written; the deliverables are the merged, overset-safe press PDFs the plugin was meant to produce.
one_line_ask: Bring eight differently-lit party-product photos to one matched look by neutralizing each to the grey card it carries, produce a seasonal colorway of the hero product without a reshoot, prep and vectorize the client wordmark, then data-merge the client's overset-safe auto-fit catalog and price-tag templates against the roster so long product names shrink to fit instead of clipping, and export press-ready PDFs.
full_brief: Larkfield Party Co. prints a per-event promotional product catalog and matching shelf price tags, one card and one tag per SKU, driven from a spreadsheet (one row per SKU: product name, blurb, price, SKU code, event name). Our recurring headache is that long product names and blurbs overflow the frame and get clipped on export — the layout won't shrink them to fit on its own. We have already rebuilt both templates ourselves in a professional page-layout program with 'auto-size / shrink text to fit frame' switched on for every variable-data frame and real merge fields wired up (ProductName, Blurb, Price, SKU, EventName), so the layouts are now overset-safe; we are handing them to you as finished template files and we do not want them redesigned. What we need from you is everything that flows INTO those templates. First, the photography: we are sending eight existing product shots and NOT reshooting. They were taken over a couple of afternoons under whatever light was around — some cool, some warm, a couple too dark or too bright — so out of the folder they look like a mismatched jumble, and a catalog of mismatched shots reads cheap. To make matched-ness checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. Bring the whole set to one consistent, true-to-product look by neutralizing each image to the grey card it contains until that card reads as a clean neutral grey; once every card is neutral the set will share one white point. Hold a subtle warm, celebratory feel in the final look, but do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch — each shot was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target, and neutralize to the CARD, not to an assumed cast: some of these products are genuinely warm-colored, and if a product's own color is already warm you must not cool it chasing a cast that isn't there, or you strip the very color we are selling. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you settled on for each frame so we can confirm the set is matched, not eyeballed. Second, a seasonal colorway without a reshoot: on the hero SKU (the foil number-balloon bundle) the ribbon is currently a bright red — give us a deeper gala-burgundy version of that same shot, a rich dark wine-red in the same color family, and the recolor has to sit under the ribbon's real folds, sheen and shadow with the rest of the product untouched — no flat dead color, no whole-image tint bleeding onto the balloons. Third, our wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper and looks fuzzy at print size — get it clean and razor-sharp as vector art so it stays crisp wherever it lands in the layouts. Finally, build the pieces: merge the roster into BOTH of our auto-fit templates — the catalog (one A4 card per SKU, carrying that SKU's graded photo and the wordmark) and the shelf tags (one small tag per SKU, carrying the wordmark) — so every row becomes its own page, long records shrink to fit via the templates' auto-size instead of clipping, and hand back two press-ready PDFs: the catalog at A4 with 3mm bleed and the tags at tag size, both ~300 DPI. Bind our copy and prices verbatim from the roster; do not rewrite them. The whole point: long records must render legibly through the templates' auto-fit, never clipped, and the photos must read as one matched set.

inputs.name: catalog_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built page-layout document (.indd / .idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A4 portrait catalog card — ONE product per page (210x297mm + 3mm bleed). It must contain live variable-data placeholder fields <<ProductName>>, <<Blurb>>, <<Price>>, <<SKU>>, <<EventName>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a product image frame bound to @ProductImage (that row's graded photo) and a masthead image frame bound to @Logo (the shared vectorized wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, both images reach the card ONLY as merge binds through these image frames. CRITICAL per the brief: every text frame holding a variable field has native 'Auto-Size / shrink text to fit frame' enabled so long merged strings shrink instead of going overset. The card's decorative background is already placed by the client inside this authored file. Built by hand so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind; explicitly NOT a pdf-to-layout conversion and NOT a multi-record grid — the merge emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd/.idml carrying real merge fields plus genuine @-image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record card is the correct, connector-doable shape. A pdf-converted layout with literal typed text will NOT bind, and a multi-up grid cannot be produced; both are the killed original design. TWO image columns (@ProductImage, @Logo) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's graded product photo AND the shared vectorized wordmark — giving the chain-produced wordmark a real, connector-doable path onto every card with no free-form placement. Field names must exactly match the CSV headers. The auto-size behavior is the client's stated requirement baked into the authored template, not something the agent can add — the agent's job is to feed field-matched data and art into it.

inputs.name: pricetag_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built page-layout document (.indd / .idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD 90x50mm shelf price tag — ONE product per page. It carries live variable-data fields <<ProductName>>, <<Price>>, <<SKU>> and ONE @-prefixed image-path merge column wired to a small logo frame bound to @Logo (the shared vectorized wordmark). The ProductName frame has native 'Auto-Size / shrink text to fit frame' enabled so a long name shrinks rather than clipping on the small tag. Built by hand so the fields and the image field bind; NOT a pdf-to-layout conversion.
inputs.realism_notes: Second [T] merge target on the SAME roster CSV. Modeled as a real page-layout .indd (NOT a vector-artwork file merged through the text-only vector-merge tool — that tool cannot bind an image column, which is why the logo could never reach a vector-merged tag; this was the audited defect). One @-image column (@Logo, the same file in every row) puts the vectorized wordmark on every tag as a merge bind. Field names match the CSV headers; the tag ignores Blurb/EventName/@ProductImage.

inputs.name: catalog_data.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate an 8-row CSV for an event / party-supply promo line with header row exactly: ProductName,Blurb,Price,SKU,EventName,@ProductImage,@Logo. One row per SKU, in this order: (1) Foil Number Balloon Bundle; (2) Confetti Cannon; (3) Paper Lantern String Set; (4) Rose-Gold Tableware Pack; (5) Metallic Streamer Twist Pack; (6) Warm-White LED Fairy String; (7) Themed Dinner Napkin Bundle; (8) Party Popper Crate. Include a deliberate mix of SHORT and DELIBERATELY LONG ProductName and Blurb strings — e.g. one name ~15 chars ('Confetti Cannon') and one ~62 chars ('Deluxe Personalised Helium-Filled Foil Number Balloon Bundle (Gold)'), and blurbs ranging from one short line to two dense keyword-rich lines — so the auto-size / overset behaviour is actually exercised. Prices like '$12.99', SKU codes like 'LKF-0142', EventName values like 'Summer Gala 2026'. The @ProductImage column names that SKU's prepped photo file (e.g. @balloon_cell.jpg) so the merge drops each graded photo into that row's card; the @Logo column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @larkfield_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row.
inputs.realism_notes: Column headers must EXACTLY match both templates' merge fields and BOTH @-image columns. The long/short length spread is the whole point — it is what triggers the shrink-to-fit the brief is about. The @Logo column is the identical vectorized SVG path in all eight rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark a connector-doable path onto every card and tag via the merge. Columns encode NO treatment triage: every @ProductImage is a same-kind graded photo file the agent names per its own grading, and nothing in the CSV telegraphs which photo needed which correction. Eight rows => each merge must produce exactly eight pages.

inputs.name: product_photos_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame camera captures of party / event promotion products, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, downscale-only from here), each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot across two afternoons under mismatched light: (1) a glossy GOLD foil number-balloon bundle tied with a bright RED satin ribbon, mixed window + warm room light, real specular highlights on the foil (HERO — feeds the ribbon recolor); (2) a confetti cannon tube, cool bluish fluorescent cast; (3) a string of paper lanterns, warm tungsten cast; (4) a rose-gold metallic tableware pack whose product color is GENUINELY warm rose-gold, shot under near-neutral light so its grey card already reads neutral (the warmth is the real product, not a white-balance error); (5) a pack of metallic streamer twists, flat and underexposed; (6) a warm-white LED fairy-light string, slightly overexposed and warm; (7) a bundle of themed dinner napkins, cool cast; (8) a crate of party poppers, near-neutral light. Every shot has real product texture, cluttered party-supply-counter surroundings, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI, no pre-cut cutout. Frames are level (no planted tilt).
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each crop can fill the catalog image cell at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame white balance and exposure vary in opposite directions) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision toward the shared grey-card white point. THE TRAP is frame 4 (rose-gold tableware): its warmth is real product color and its grey card is already neutral, so the correct move is NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness); a naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' move used on frames 2/7, or that 'cools an imagined blue cast', pushes its card off-neutral and strips the product's real color. Frame 1 carries the bright red ribbon for the masked recolor and must be neutralized before it feeds that branch. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution stills.

inputs.name: larkfield_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'LARKFIELD' event-brand wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a bold geometric sans in a deep ink color with a small confetti-burst mark, solid flat fills, no gradients. Rendered as a real scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will trace into crisp vector geometry.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so a raw trace would bake in the paper rectangle and the skew — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, boost contrast/crispness, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. The wordmark's enclosed letter counters stay filled by remove_background (it isolates only the outer ground), but the catalog masthead and tag are LIGHT, so the counters read white and the mark is correct — no dark-ground knockout is claimed. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering.

outputs.name: catalog_merged_print.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly EIGHT press-ready A4 portrait catalog cards — ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row data-merge; each card binds its ProductName/Blurb/Price/SKU/EventName verbatim from the roster with that SKU's grey-card-neutralized photo dropped into the product image frame (via @ProductImage) and the vectorized wordmark dropped into the masthead frame (via @Logo), both by merge bind, never free-form placement. Long ProductName/Blurb records render shrunk-to-fit via the template's auto-size (no overset clipping). 210x297mm + 3mm bleed, ~300 DPI.

outputs.name: pricetags_merged.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly EIGHT press-ready 90x50mm shelf price tags — one per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the second one-file-per-row data-merge; each tag binds ProductName/Price/SKU verbatim and the vectorized wordmark via @Logo. Long names auto-size to fit the small tag frame instead of clipping.

outputs.name: graded_product_photos_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized party-product photos, delivered as the catalog-cell crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge via @ProductImage, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (in-frame 18% grey card present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within ~3 levels) with the whole set matched to one shared white point while holding a subtle warm celebratory tone, and true-to-product (no product's genuine color forced off); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered cell crop (grey card fully cropped OUT). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Accompanied by the agent's report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame.

outputs.name: variant_balloon_gala.jpg
outputs.spec: Seasonal colorway of the hero foil-balloon shot: the bright red satin ribbon deepened to the gala-burgundy house color via a masked, luminosity-preserving pair of hue/saturation/luminance passes (a small within-family hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance drop that darkens and mutes the red — an in-band adjacent shift, no near-complementary rotation) riding the ribbon's existing luminosity, so its folds, sheen highlights and cast shadow stay natural and the balloons are untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill.

outputs.name: larkfield_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead and tag scale with no captured paper ground or skew, reading correctly on the light catalog and tag.

connector_workflow.note: Neutralize this frame to its in-frame 18% grey card by eye: dial temperature/tint until the card reads a clean neutral grey, then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey and hold a subtle warm celebratory tone. Reason the values to THIS card; report the final white-balance and exposure move. Keep this full-res neutralized master (card in frame) — it is retained for grading and also feeds the colorway branch. Single primitive-built adjustments call.

Crop the neutralized frame to the catalog image-cell aspect the card expects, framing on the product with the grey card cropped OUT — this crop binds into the card via @ProductImage. The pre-crop master (balloon_neutralized, card in frame) is retained as the grading artifact; neutrality is graded there, card-exclusion is the separate check here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand.

Neutralize this frame to its own in-frame grey card by eye and land it on the shared white point set on frame 1; set exposure to match the set brightness, hold the warm tone. Reason the values to THIS card — do not reuse another frame's numbers. Report the move.
Crop to the catalog image cell, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Neutralize this frame to its in-frame grey card by eye onto the shared white point; set exposure to match set brightness and hold the warm tone. Report the move.
Crop to the catalog image cell, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Neutralize this frame to its OWN in-frame grey card by eye, then match set brightness. Decide the white-balance from THIS card, not from the batch — if the card already reads neutral, do not push it. Report the move you settled on.
Crop to the catalog image cell, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Neutralize this frame to its in-frame grey card by eye onto the shared white point; judge the exposure/contrast this frame needs so it matches the set's brightness. Report the move.
Crop to the catalog image cell, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Neutralize this frame to its in-frame grey card by eye onto the shared white point; recover the brightest areas so nothing stays blown, then match set brightness. Report the move.
Crop to the catalog image cell, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Neutralize this frame to its in-frame grey card by eye onto the shared white point; keep the printed napkin colors true. Report the move.
Crop to the catalog image cell, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Neutralize this frame to its in-frame grey card by eye onto the shared white point; judge how small a correction it needs so the set converges. Report the move. Frames 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own card.
Crop to the catalog image cell, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

On the neutralized full-res hero, semantically select only the ribbon ('the red satin ribbon tied around the foil balloon bundle') so the colorway is confined to the ribbon and the balloons stay untouched. Returns a maskURI — a real object, not a hue or coordinate region.

Masked colorway pass 1 (consumes hero + ribbon mask): move the ribbon toward the gala-burgundy target while keeping it in the red family — a small within-band hue nudge plus a luminance drop that darkens the satin, letting the ribbon's existing luminosity carry the folds, sheen and shadow. Confined to the mask; stay well inside the red/wine band.

Masked colorway pass 2 (same mask): trim the red-band saturation and settle the luminance so the ribbon lands on the deep gala-burgundy house target rather than a flat brick or a still-bright candy red, still riding the original luminosity so the satin sheen and shadow stay natural. A deepen-and-mute in the same family.
Resize the finished gala-burgundy colorway to the same web/catalog frame as the set. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Prep-before-trace step 1: rectify the scan's residual rotation so the vector edges come out square. Feeding the raw scan to the tracer would bake in the skew — image_auto_straighten is the only tool that rectifies a tilt.
Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the off-white paper toward white so the ink separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so the tracer sees only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white outer paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (never select->invert->fill). The enclosed letter counters remain filled — correct here because the catalog masthead and tag are light, so they read white.

Trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead and tag. Tracing the raw scan instead would yield a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette, which the prep chain is there to avoid.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: balloon_cell, confetti_cell, lantern_cell, tableware_cell, streamer_cell, fairy_cell, napkins_cell, poppers_cell, larkfield_wordmark.svg
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the eight neutralized catalog-cell photos plus the vector wordmark so both merges can resolve them by the @ProductImage column (per-row photo) and the @Logo column (shared mark). Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references (e.g. larkfield_wordmark.svg for @Logo).
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @ProductImage and @Logo columns resolve to for each single-record page.

One-file-per-row data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (ProductName/Blurb/Price/SKU/EventName) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD catalog .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row — that row's graded photo into the @ProductImage frame AND the vectorized wordmark (from @Logo, the same SVG every row) into the masthead frame — producing EXACTLY ONE card per row (eight pages). The template's auto-size frames shrink long records (the brief's overset fix); the agent cannot shrink text itself, only route field-matched data + art into the authored auto-fit template. [T] requires the hand-authored template with its two merge-wired image frames.

Export the merged cards to press-ready ~300 DPI A4 + 3mm bleed PDF — the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight cards, one page per SKU) in a single call; it cannot export one named record on its own. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

Second one-file-per-row data-merge on the SAME roster: bind ProductName/Price/SKU into the authored single-record tag .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve the @Logo image column (shared vectorized wordmark) into the tag's logo frame — one 90x50mm tag per row (eight pages). The name frame's auto-size shrinks long names to fit. [T] on the hand-authored tag template.
Export the merged tags to press-ready PDF — the whole merged document (all eight tags, one per SKU) in a single call. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Eight per-photo grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization (adaptive per frame — the light differs shot to shot and one product is genuinely warm, so each needs its own decision toward the same shared white point) followed by a catalog-cell crop, with the pre-crop neutralized masters (card still in frame) retained by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifacts. The hero's neutralized full-res frame (balloon_neutralized, step 1) feeds BOTH its cell crop (step 2) AND the colorway branch: image_select_by_prompt(17) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(18) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(19) -> resize(20), the two HSL passes both consuming ribbon_mask. The wordmark runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: image_auto_straighten(21) -> crisp adjustments(22) -> image_crop_to_bounds(23) -> image_remove_background to transparency(24) -> image_vectorize(25). The eight cell crops and the wordmark SVG converge into the upload session(26) -> finalize(27), then the SAME uploaded URNs and the SAME roster CSV drive two merges: document_merge_data_layout into the authored catalog .indd(28) -> document_render_layout(29) for the catalog PDF, and document_merge_data_layout into the authored tag .indd(30) -> document_render_layout(31) for the tags PDF. Each merge resolves the @ProductImage column (that row's graded photo, catalog only) and the @Logo column (the shared vectorized wordmark, identical every row) into the templates' merge-wired image frames — the only connector-doable path for the images since free-form placement is banned. Nothing after the raw loads originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 31 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (cool frames warmed, warm frames cooled, one genuinely warm product held, one underexposed frame lifted, one overexposed frame recovered) all forced to converge on a single measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass. Layered on top: a masked luminosity-preserving ribbon colorway (a within-family bright-red -> gala-burgundy deepen, an in-band adjacent shift image_adjust_hsl can actually hold — no near-complementary rotation) as two HSL passes; a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white scan; and a TWO-format one-file-per-row data-merge into TWO hand-authored auto-fit templates (the row's graded photo via @ProductImage and the shared vectorized wordmark via @Logo, so both images reach the page as merge binds rather than banned free-form placement). Recognizing the overset complaint cannot be 'fixed' by the agent — only routed into the client's auto-size templates — plus exact field-name/column alignment between CSV, both .indd field sets and both @-image columns, is the reasoning the job rewards. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used and the text-only document_merge_data_vector is NOT used to bind an image; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; deprecated image_adjust_* names are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every product photo carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance target is that each frame's card, graded on its RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master, reads a clean neutral with the whole set matched to one white point — a target the agent can miss, and it must REPORT the final white-balance and exposure move per frame so 'matched' is verifiable, not asserted. The agent works by EYE and reports the parameters it applied; it never reads a pixel value. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit shots to a common white point, each needing its own opposite-direction correction, not one blanket pass; (2) a masked, luminosity-preserving bright-red -> gala-burgundy ribbon colorway (a within-family deepen-and-mute an adjacent-hue image_adjust_hsl shift can reliably hold, not a near-complementary rotation) that must keep satin sheen and shadow natural using the only masked recolor path (image_adjust_hsl), not image_apply_color_overlay (whole-image) or image_fill_area (flat dead-fill); (3) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed, off-white, margin-padded wordmark scan (straighten -> crisp -> crop-to-bounds -> knock-to-transparency) before vectorize. TRAP: the rose-gold tableware (frame 4) is genuinely warm-colored and was shot under near-neutral light, so its grey card is already neutral — the naive path batch-applies the same 'warm the cool cast' move used on the cool frames (or 'cools an imagined blue cast'), pushing its card off-neutral and stripping the real product color; the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. A second trap sits in the merge: a pdf-converted layout template or a multi-record grid both fail to bind/produce, and the text-only vector-merge tool cannot carry the logo image — only the two supplied single-record authored .indd templates with @-image columns merge correctly.
